author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.
decisions:

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can filter the veterinarian list by specialty
summary: Both veterinarian list surfaces, the paged HTML directory and the reinstated machine-readable list, accept an optional specialty in the address and list only veterinarians holding it. Without one, both behave as today.
acceptance_criteria: GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only vets holding that specialty; pagination (page count, page content) applies to the filtered list
On a filtered /vets.html page, the pagination links carry the specialty parameter so every linked page stays filtered
GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns only vets holding that specialty; the response stays unpaged, as today
Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive: 'RADIOLOGY' matches radiology; a prefix such as 'radio' matches no vet (PRD REQ-VET-001 edge cases 3-4)
A specialty no vet holds, known or unknown, yields HTTP 200 with the normal page or JSON document and an empty vet list (edge case 5)
An empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves as if the parameter were absent, on both endpoints (edge case 6)
Without the parameter, /vets.html and /vets behave exactly as today
A vet holding several specialties appears once in a filtered list; a vet holding none appears in no filtered list (edge cases 7-8)
Neither surface gains a form, dropdown, or other page control for the filter
non_goals: Free-text search for veterinarians, pets, or visits (NG-9, narrowed)
Any form, dropdown, or other page control for the filter on either surface (owner-deferred to a possible follow-up request)
Filtering by more than one specialty in one request (PRD open question; no promise made)
Trimming spaces around a non-empty specialty value (PRD open question; no promise made)
notes: REQ-VET-003 is the fresh requirement for the reinstated machine-readable list (/vets), per the owner's decision; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and is not reused. The HTML filter is tagged REQ-VET-001 in docs/prd.md, since it extends that requirement's page. Both surfaces ship in one slice: one behavior (one matching rule) on one code surface, estimated at 6-8 TDD cycles. The query parameter name 'specialty' is the owner's stated URL contract. Narrowest readings taken where open (recorded in PRD Open Questions): repeated specialty values and surrounding spaces on non-empty values carry no promise. docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for the new non-goal ADR; it is outside this agent's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package unchanged (system-design § Package Structure; no service layer, controller -> repository per the feature-package ADR). Small adjustment, now recorded in § Contracts: VetRepository gains specialty-filtered reads (paged for the HTML directory, unpaged for the machine-readable list) that are not cached; VetController binds an optional `specialty` request parameter on /vets.html and /vets and normalizes blank or all-space to absent (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row: normalization is binding). Placement, recorded in the § Contracts invariant prose: the matching rule (whole name, ignoring letter case, each vet once) lives in VetRepository's queries, the one home both surfaces share, never in the controller or the template. New § Scale and Load row for the veterinarian directory. Vets, VetController, VetRepository, and CacheConfiguration rows now carry REQ-VET-003; the Known Defects row for the unconsumed machine-readable route is removed because REQ-VET-003 now governs that route. Basis: code read by grep/cat (IDE oracle not connected; weaker basis): VetController.java, VetRepository.java, Vet.java, vetList.html, CacheConfiguration.java, db/h2/data.sql.
integration_points: Binding, GET /vets.html: `specialty` binds as an optional request-scoped String (@RequestParam, not required) alongside the existing `page` int; no persisted type is bound. The normalized value is put into the model so the template can build pagination links
Binding, GET /vets: the same optional request-scoped String `specialty`; response stays the unpaged Vets wrapper, with the same JSON shape as today

Repository boundary, VetRepository: the matching rule is exercised against the real H2 database through a @DataJpaTest (new VetRepositoryTests, or extend ClinicServiceTests), with fixture vets inserted in the test transaction where paging needs more than one page of a specialty (the seed holds at most two vets per specialty against a page size of five). No double for the matching rule: a double would have to re-implement the rule

Framework transport, VetControllerTests: MockMvc (the sanctioned harness). The existing @MockitoBean VetRepository stub may stay for the controller tests; reason: they assert only binding, blank normalization, forwarding of the specialty to the right repository method, pagination-link rendering, and response shape, never the matching rule. A hand-written VetRepository double is equally acceptable
Template, vetList.html: pagination links carry the specialty when present and stay identical to today's links when absent

patterns.description: blank search parameter treated as the broadest search; mirror for specialty (blank or all-space -> absent). Surrounding spaces on a non-empty value carry no promise (PRD Open Question): do not strip a non-empty value
paged Spring Data query with a parameter; the filtered vet query is an explicit parameterized JPQL query

risks.risk: Template expression injection: the existing pagination links use Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) inside string-concatenated URLs. Putting the request-derived specialty through preprocessing would evaluate caller input as an expression
risks.mitigation: Build every link with link-expression parameters, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encode the value; never place `specialty` inside __${...}__ (security-principles § Realization, injection row and fail-secure principle). With no specialty, the links must render exactly as today; assert both cases in a test

risks.risk: Query injection, and prefix leakage through LIKE wildcards: a LIKE-based match would let '%' or '_' in the value widen the match, breaking the whole-name rule (PRD REQ-VET-001 edge case 4)
risks.mitigation: Equality on lower-cased names with a bound parameter (e.g. JPQL `lower(s.name) = lower(:specialty)`); no LIKE and no string concatenation (security-principles § Realization, injection row; system-design § Threat Model, SQL injection row). LOWER on both sides behaves the same on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, so the case-insensitive defect seen in PostgreSQL owner search (Known Defects) does not recur here

risks.risk: Duplicate rows and wrong page counts: a join over vet_specialties can return a vet once per matching specialty and miscount pages
risks.mitigation: Select distinct vets, and give the paged query an explicit count query that counts distinct vets (system-design § Scale and Load row, Form column). Matching is on one specialty name, so a vet appears at most once; still assert that each vet appears once (PRD edge case 7)

risks.risk: Unbounded cache growth: the vet cache uses method arguments as its key and has no size bound, so caching filtered reads would let callers grow it with arbitrary specialty strings
risks.mitigation: Filtered repository methods carry no @Cacheable (system-design § Contracts VetRepository row; § Scale and Load row, Limits). Unfiltered reads keep their existing caching unchanged

risks.risk: Veterinarian directory path scales with data
risks.mitigation: § Scale and Load row: bounded, so use the simplest readable form, one parameterized query per filtered request

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to audit. Design-doc writes this dispatch: docs/system-design.md (Contracts invariant prose and rows for Vets, VetRepository, VetController, CacheConfiguration; new § Scale and Load; Security Context inputs; Threat Model SQL-injection row wording; removed the resolved Known Defects row) and docs/adr/README.md (index row for the 2026-10-24 NG-9 narrowing ADR, as the product expert flagged). No new ADR: no decision here constrains later slices beyond what one current-state line carries. Effort rated involved for the template-injection and distinct-count subtleties, despite the adjacent owner-search seam. No form, dropdown, or page control on either surface (owner decision). Multiple specialty values and surrounding-space trimming carry no promise: take Spring's default binding of a single value and do not add handling for either. The prd-entry file_targets omit a repository-level test; the matching tests belong there (VetRepositoryTests or ClinicServiceTests), not only in stubbed controller tests.

findings.description: The conditional `${specialty == null} ? @{/vets.html(page=...)} : @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}` is repeated across the five pagination links (page numbers, first, previous, next, last). author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-derived specialty reaches JPQL only as a bound named parameter (VetRepository.java: `WHERE lower(specialty.name) = lower(:specialty)` with `@Param("specialty")`) on both findBySpecialty overloads and the countQuery; no string-concatenated query text carries request input. Equality rather than LIKE also keeps '%' and '_' from widening the match.

Cache-key exhaustion avoided: the two new repository methods are deliberately not @Cacheable, so a caller-supplied specialty cannot grow the unbounded 'vets' cache (VetRepository.java javadoc: `Not cached: the key would be caller-supplied and the vet cache is unbounded`).

Output escaping and template-expression safety: the request-derived specialty is rendered in vets/vetList.html only inside Thymeleaf link expressions as a link parameter (`@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`), which URL-encodes the value, and th:href attribute-escapes it; it is never emitted as text or unescaped markup. The change also removes the five `__${...}__` preprocessing uses from the vet pagination links; `grep -rn -F -e '__${' src/main/resources/templates` finds none left in vets/, and the remaining hits (owners/ownersList.html, fragments/*) are pre-existing, untouched by this diff, and carry server-side values, not request text.

Input handling at the boundary: specialty is an optional @RequestParam String; blank or whitespace-only collapses to no filter (VetController.presentOrNull), matching PRD REQ-VET-003 edge case 6. No new exception path is introduced, so no new message can reach the error page that renders exception text. Result size is bounded by the existing findAll surface (a filtered list is a subset of the unfiltered one).

Exposed surface: no new route; the existing GET /vets.html and GET /vets gain a read-only filter parameter. No mutation, no new binding target (no @ModelAttribute/@RequestBody added), so mass-assignment rows are unaffected. No secrets, credentials, logging, file I/O, process execution or deserialization added in the diff.

Supply chain: build.gradle and the gradle/ and settings files are unchanged in this diff (`git diff --stat` empty); OWASP Dependency-Check is not configured (`grep -i dependencycheck build.gradle` no match), so no NVD match ran in this review. Resolved versions from `./gradlew dependencies`: Spring Boot 4.1.1, Spring Data JPA 4.1.1, Hibernate ORM 7.4.5.Final, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, Jackson databind 3.1.5 (tools.jackson).

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The paged findBySpecialty(String, Pageable) carries its own copy of the WHERE clause in @Query and countQuery (VetRepository.java: `WHERE lower(specialty.name) = lower(:specialty)` appears in the query and again in the countQuery), and it is the query behind the HTML directory, the primary surface. The case-insensitivity, prefix-no-match and wildcard-literal cases (PRD edge cases 3 and 4) run only against the unpaged Collection variant. The paged variant is exercised only with the exact-case name (pagination, distinct) and with names that match nothing (empty). Dropping lower() or switching to LIKE in the paged query or its countQuery would leave every test green, because the controller tests stub the repository. Checked with grep -F -e findBySpecialty over src/test: the Page overload is called only in VetRepositoryTests and stubbed in VetControllerTests.
findings.fix: Run the other-case, prefix and wildcard assertions against the Page overload too, for example by asserting both variants in the same test (the empty-list test already does) and checking getTotalElements for the other-case match.

recommendations: theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchOnlyTheWholeNameIgnoringCase asserts two unrelated cases (other case, prefix) in one test; splitting would give each edge case its own failure name.
VetControllerTests relies on @MockitoBean for the repository, which the brief tolerates; no new framework double type was introduced beyond what the host file already uses.
approved_aspects: Specialty matching rule is tested at VetRepository against the real database (@DataJpaTest, Replace.NONE), where system-design.md places it; the controller tests cover only blank normalization, pass-through and link shaping, which the design assigns to the controller

coverage-map: both Done-when bullets and all 8 declared tests are present; PRD edge cases 3 to 8 each have a test (case, prefix, unheld, blank, multi-specialty once, no-specialty vet excluded in theSpecialtyFilterShouldListOnlyVetsHoldingTheRequestedSpecialty)
./gradlew test passes (BUILD SUCCESSFUL; only the MySQL and Postgres container tests skipped)
Names follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school, AssertJ is used in the repository tests, and test data goes through createAVet/createASpecialty factories with named constants

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Fix-delta scope: read via `python3 scripts/changeset.py --base-tree 5f90a967b0bf8bf7695885432d18aaa798501c15` (7 files: 4 docs, VetRepository.java, vets/vetList.html, VetRepositoryTests.java). I had no open findings from round 1 (record line 16, approved).

Data access stays parameterized: the repository refactor only moves the JPQL into compile-time constants (VetRepository.java `String SPECIALTY_FROM = " FROM Vet vet JOIN vet.specialties specialty" + " WHERE lower(specialty.name) = lower(:specialty)";`) composed into `@Query(SPECIALTY_MATCH + " ORDER BY vet.id")` and `countQuery = SPECIALTY_COUNT`. Annotation values must be compile-time constants, so no request text can reach the query string. The request value still binds only through `@Param("specialty")`, and equality matching means '%' and '_' are not treated as wildcards.

Replaced URL control is equal strength: round 1 relied on link-expression parameter encoding (`@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`). The delta builds the suffix as `'&specialty=' + ${#uris.escapeQueryParam(specialty)}` (vetList.html:27) and appends it to a context-relative `@{/vets.html(page=...)}`. escapeQueryParam percent-encodes '&', '=', '#', '+', '"', '<', '>' and space, so the value cannot add parameters or break the attribute, and th:href HTML-escapes the attribute output. The href always starts with the app-relative path, so no scheme (`javascript:`) can be injected. VetControllerTests.java:161 `theVetDirectoryPaginationLinksShouldEncodeTheSpecialtyRatherThanEvaluateIt` asserts a hostile value `__${1+1}__&page=9` renders as `__$%7B1%2B1%7D__%26page%3D9` after `&`; per build-pass line 28 the suite passes.

Template-expression safety: the delta adds no `__${...}__` preprocessing in vets/vetList.html. Checked with `grep -rn -F -e '#uris' src/main/resources/templates` (only hit: vetList.html:27) and a th:href sweep of the templates. Remaining `__${` uses in owners/ and fragments/ predate this slice, are untouched, and carry server-side values.

Pattern consistency: no other template puts request-supplied text into a URL (th:href sweep: owners/ownersList.html pagination concatenates only server-side integers). So there is no neighboring encoding pattern this one diverges from.

Docs delta (prd.md, system-design.md, ubiquitous-language.md, ADR) is vocabulary only ('narrowing' renamed to 'Specialty filter'). It changes no security statement, trust boundary, or threat-model row. No secrets were added; the added lines are JPQL fragments, template expressions, tests, and prose.

Supply chain: build.gradle and pom.xml are not in the fix delta, so the dependency set is unchanged since round 1. I did not re-run `./gradlew dependencies` this round, and no NVD match ran because dependencyCheckAnalyze is not run by this review.

author: change-grader
summary: add optional specialty filter to both vet list surfaces

blast_radius.note: Three production files in the one vet package (controller, repository, template) plus PRD, design, vocabulary and a new non-goal ADR; no sensitive paths, and the unfiltered read paths and their cache annotations are untouched.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every prod hunk: the filter is a bound-parameter JPQL equality on lower(name) with DISTINCT and a matching count query, blank input normalizes to the existing findAll paths, and the one hand-assembled spot (the '&specialty=' tail in vetList.html) goes through #uris.escapeQueryParam and is pinned by a hostile-value test; nothing behaves differently from what the request describes.

test_adequacy.note: VetRepositoryTests runs both overloads against real H2 for case-insensitivity, prefix and wildcard non-match, distinct-once, empty results and second-page content and totals; controller tests drive the real MVC and template for links, encoding, blank values and the unchanged unfiltered output. The one gap is that no test wires the controller to the real repository, though each layer is covered on its own.

reviewer_hedging.note: Round 1 had three changes_requested (query and link duplication, paged-overload test gap, doc vocabulary), all addressed. The round-2 approvals are clean but carry two polish recommendations: the SPECIALTY_* query constants are public interface members and SPECIALTY_FROM's name understates that it holds the WHERE clause, and the Scale and Load row restates a seed count that will go stale. Both are low-stakes.

scope_deviation.note: Every scope move (narrowing NG-9 with an ADR, minting REQ-VET-003 while REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn, URL-only filter, pagination carrying the parameter) is quoted from the intake decision, and the unresolved points went in as recorded open questions. The row says design_revisions 0 and build_retries 0, yet the log has three minor design-blocks and one build-failure; those were fix-round prose and vocabulary passes and a truncation checkpoint, not real revisions or red builds.

rationale: Code and tests are tight and in scope; the only flag is the round-2 approvals' residual polish. Skim the diff, then decide whether to make VetRepository's public SPECIALTY_* constants less visible and to drop the seed count from system-design's Scale and Load row before merge or as a follow-up.
